correctness.rationale: The exact first integral y²/(1+3x²)+[log(1+3x²)-2/(1+3x²)+2]/9 was independently differentiated against dx/dt=(1+3x²)y and dy/dt=-x-x³+3xy², yielding identically zero. U is even and strictly increasing for x>0, so all E>0 levels are compact noncritical ovals. Original-time quadrature uses |dx/dt|=P^(3/2)*sqrt(E-U), and T=4I_0, M_q=I_q/I_0. Under v=U(x), g_q(v)=x^(q-1)*sqrt(P)/(2(1+x²)); near v=0 it is ~v^((q-1)/2)/2, and at infinity ~sqrt(3)x^(q-2)/2. The Abel kernel gives integrable q<2 beta constants, critical q=2: M2~3E, and q>2: M_q~A_E^(q-2)*sqrt(pi E/[2(q-2)]). A_E~exp((9E-2)/2)/sqrt(3); T~4/sqrt(3E); the density is sqrt(3)/(2P^(3/2)). Crucially fixed q precedes E->infinity. I checked the beta normalization at q=0 and the use of physical rather than reparametrized time.
